overall: The AG found the committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to create and timely approve twelve sets of workshop and special meeting minutes, and ordered future compliance; the response-timeliness and post-complaint minutes issues were not reached.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to respond to two requests (Nov. 2023 and Mar. 2024) for open and executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: As a preliminary matter, we decline to review allegations that the Committee failed to timely or properly respond to the two requests for meeting minutes, as such allegations were not timely filed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to create, maintain, and timely approve minutes of workshop, budget, and special meetings held 2020-2023.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when it did not approve twelve sets of minutes—for meetings ranging from September 2020 through May 2024—until August 27, 2024, which was more than 30 days and three meetings following each meeting.

allegations.summary: Concerns that minutes created after the complaint was filed with the committee were insufficient were raised only with the AG, not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not address concerns raised with this office that some meeting minutes, which were first created and provided to Mr. Maccioli well after the complaint was filed with the Committee, are insufficient.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law and may result in the imposition of civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
